summary: @servicetitan/component-usage ships install-time Bun-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs', which auto-runs on npm install. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime binary from GitHub releases (oven-sh/bun) to a temp directory, chmods it executable (mode 0755), and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB heavily obfuscated JavaScript blob (header '// @bun @bun-cjs', rotating string-array obfuscator with hex-named identifiers and no human-readable logic) whose executable content cannot be inspected. The legitimate-looking dist/index.js referencing @servicetitan/design-system and @servicetitan/anvil2 is a cover for the install-time dropper. The package is published to the public npm registry under the @servicetitan scope, consistent with a dependency-confusion attack against ServiceTitan's private scope: installers in ServiceTitan's build chain that resolve @servicetitan/component-usage from the public registry will pull this artifact and execute the obfuscated payload under Bun with the installer's privileges. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern — fetching a second runtime at install time to execute an opaque payload evades Node-based scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
